lead: the hospital run was yours for six years and there is no evening on which you agreed to it. when the weather turned it went out with the whole of that life, and there was nobody to hand it to.
sun: your endings work by removal, and removal assumes the thing was joined to you. the trade was joined to you. the run was not — it belonged to whoever set it down, and a season cannot lift what was never attached. so the ending took the whole of what was yours and left a dozen services running in your name for a life already gone.
moon: the assumption does the work. people see space, put the thing there, and by the second month it is a fixed arrangement with no conversation behind it. nothing in you registers the moment as an addition, so you cannot date one of them either, and when the weather goes there is no paper to produce that would separate what you took on from what was simply left with you.
pull: the run was never once put to you as a question. when you finished with that town, the run is what everybody decided you had finally had enough of.
tension: an explanation was waiting for you before you went. people who watched that run for six years read the leaving as the run finally telling — worn out, put upon, a man who did too much and cracked. what happened was a season ending and taking everything in it, the run with the job. so you are recorded there as somebody who resented them quietly for years, and the ones who set the most down are surest of it.
cost: a new place has you doing something real inside two months, nobody appointing you, because whatever it needs finds the space and settles in. one item in twelve years was put to you and taken on out loud, and you have kept it at full weight through two complete endings — and to anybody who has watched you carry things it is indistinguishable from the rest of the load.

lead: a man two lives behind you told you the worst thing he has done, once, in a parked car, and you hold it in his own words — and you could not name the street he lived on.
sun: when a life goes here it goes whole, and what people told you is the one thing the fortnight cannot reach. a thing said to you was never yours, so it is not on the list of what comes off. everything that could be shed went at one speed. what they said sat where it was, at the volume it went in at, and has outlived your acquaintance with all of them.
moon: the ear takes delivery whether or not a thing was sent, and what it takes does not thin with distance. the holdings keep their original weight: the confession at one in the morning, the diagnosis before the family had it, the sentence somebody has since decided was dealt with. none came with terms — terms would have needed the telling to be an arrangement, and it was a moment.
pull: you are the only living holder of the worst thing about four people you would not recognise in the street. the acquaintance ended in a fortnight; the keeping did not get a term.
tension: your standing in any room is that you hear what it is actually running on, so an ending of yours cannot be taken at face value. you left that department because the season finished. what the department concluded was that you had heard something, and two good people resigned behind you inside the year on a reading you never made — and both are certain to this day that you did them a kindness by going first.
cost: a thing told to you once is in the same condition eleven years later, never repeated, not once used in an argument it would have won. holding it is not work and it does not finish, and it does not end when the life around it does. a man rings every winter, not out of fondness, and you take it, because whoever told you that is owed it permanently.

lead: you put the usual out on the usual night and what came home was thin, and thin again the week after. by the following month you had finished with the place, on a reading taken off other people's flat season.
sun: there is one way available to you for finding out where you are, and it is to put something out and count what returns. that is also the only instrument you have for establishing that a season is over, and what it produces is total: the count stops, the whole apparatus goes with it inside a fortnight, and nothing in the way you finish things makes room for the reading having been wrong.
moon: the instrument reads the room's condition, not yours, and a room is full of people having their own bad months. it also cannot idle — a rhythm exists only while somebody produces it — so you were emitting at full through the winter you were deciding, and everybody there set their week by a count coming off a man three-quarters gone. the beat went last, with the rest.
pull: the room kept perfect time off you the whole winter you were working out that it was over, and the reading you left on was made of their tiredness, not yours.
tension: what gets said afterwards is that there was no sign, and that is accurate — output here does not report on your state, and it held its level to the final week. two of those readings were taken in a season when everyone near you was flat for their own reasons, and an ending of yours has no version that can be reopened. no instrument you own will tell you which one that was.
cost: the week a place stops answering is the week you go, so no life of yours has run on for years after it was over. what carries out of each is a rhythm rather than a person. a call at the same hour every week goes to one man from the first of them, produced for eleven years because it is owed, and taken at his end as devotion.

lead: the offer was made across a kitchen table in a house that no longer exists, deliberately, on a particular evening, to somebody you are otherwise finished with. it has moved twice since, at full size.
sun: you burn the setting. the house goes, the town goes, the arrangement of a life goes inside a fortnight — and the setting was what you made room in. so the welcome gets honoured out of whatever the next life happens to have, a smaller flat, a room a lodger has midweek, and honoured at the size promised, because a thing said out loud is what your endings are not permitted to touch.
moon: an offer here is a made object with a date on it, and what goes into the space binds at both ends, so the offering does not lapse when the life it was made in does. you have said the sentence six times in twenty years, each on purpose, and all six are live — which leaves your spare capacity committed to people out of lives you demolished yourself.
pull: every bed you have promised is promised to somebody from a life you personally finished, and the people in your kitchen tonight have been offered nothing, because the offering happened before them.
tension: you were the address in that town, the place people came to between flats and after bad news, then you were gone inside a month, and the coldest reading available is that the welcome had been a habit rather than a position. each of them kept their offer, and it left with you. two have used it since, at an address they had to be given twice, and both arrived apologising for the distance.
cost: you can put a whole life down without anybody being asked to house you, and the welcome opens again in the next place inside a month, at the same width. what is actually held — the room kept, the week cleared, the sentence meant permanently — belongs to people you are done with, and whoever is in front of you has a house whose capacity was allocated before they arrived.
